subject: Biology SL
title: Biology SL Paper 2 Section A Mock v3

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Carbon dioxide uptake was measured at different light intensities under low and high carbon dioxide concentrations.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Compare the effect of increasing light intensity on carbon dioxide uptake at low and high carbon dioxide concentration.
markscheme: At both carbon dioxide concentrations, increasing light intensity increases carbon dioxide uptake at low to moderate light intensities.
The increase is much greater at high carbon dioxide concentration; at low carbon dioxide concentration uptake approaches a lower plateau.
markschemeJa: どちらのCO₂濃度でも、低〜中光強度では光強度上昇によりCO₂取り込みが増える。
高CO₂濃度では増加が大きく、低CO₂濃度ではより低い値で頭打ちになる。
parts.modelAnswer: Increasing light raises carbon dioxide uptake in both treatments, but the response is much larger at high carbon dioxide concentration and the low-carbon-dioxide treatment reaches a lower plateau.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 光強度を上げると両条件でCO₂取り込みが増えますが、高CO₂濃度の方が増加が大きく、低CO₂濃度では低い値で頭打ちになります。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Calculate the percentage increase in carbon dioxide uptake when light intensity rises from 3 to 9 relative units at high carbon dioxide concentration.
markscheme: Increase = 11.6 − 5.1 = 6.5 relative units.
Percentage increase = 6.5 ÷ 5.1 × 100 ≈ 127%.
parts.modelAnswer: The increase is 6.5 units, so the percentage increase is 6.5 ÷ 5.1 × 100 ≈ 127%.

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain why increasing carbon dioxide concentration has little effect at the lowest light intensity.
markscheme: At very low light intensity, light-dependent reactions provide limited ATP and reducing power for carbon fixation.
Light is therefore the main limiting factor under these conditions.
Additional carbon dioxide cannot be used at a much higher rate until light availability increases.
markschemeJa: 非常に低い光強度では、光依存反応が炭素固定に必要なATPと還元力を十分に供給できない。
この条件では光が主要な制限要因である。
光量が増えるまではCO₂を追加してもより高い速度で利用できない。
parts.modelAnswer: At the lowest light intensity, light limits the supply of energy and reducing power from the light-dependent reactions. Extra carbon dioxide therefore has little effect until more light is available.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 最も低い光強度では、光依存反応から得られるエネルギーと還元力が制限されるため、CO₂を増やしても効果が小さくなります。

parts.label: (d)
parts.question: Predict the effect of increasing carbon dioxide concentration further at a light intensity of 9 relative units.
markscheme: If carbon dioxide is still limiting at high light, uptake may increase further when more carbon dioxide is supplied.
The increase would eventually become small or stop when another factor such as enzyme capacity, temperature or light becomes limiting.
markschemeJa: 高光強度でなおCO₂が制限要因なら、CO₂濃度をさらに上げると取り込みが増える可能性がある。
やがて酵素能力、温度、光など別の要因が制限要因となり、増加は小さくなるか停止する。
parts.modelAnswer: Uptake may rise further if carbon dioxide remains limiting, but it should eventually level off when another factor becomes limiting.
parts.modelAnswerJa: CO₂がまだ制限要因なら取り込みはさらに増えますが、別の要因が制限要因になると最終的に頭打ちになります。

parts.label: (e)
parts.question: Evaluate the design of the investigation and suggest improvements that would strengthen the conclusion.
markscheme: Important variables such as temperature, leaf area, plant age/water status and measurement time should be controlled when comparing treatments.
Replicate measurements should be made at each light and carbon dioxide combination and means/variation should be reported.
Using more light intensities and/or more carbon dioxide concentrations would show the response curve and limiting-factor transitions more precisely.
markschemeJa: 処理間を比較する際、温度、葉面積、植物齢・水分状態、測定時間など重要な変数を一定にする必要がある。
各光強度・CO₂濃度の組み合わせで反復測定を行い、平均とばらつきを示すべきである。
より多くの光強度やCO₂濃度を調べると、応答曲線や制限要因の移行をより正確に判断できる。
parts.modelAnswer: The investigation should control factors such as temperature, leaf area and water status. Replicates are needed to assess variation, and additional light and carbon dioxide levels would define the response more precisely.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 温度、葉面積、水分状態などを一定にし、各条件で反復測定を行う必要があります。さらに光強度やCO₂濃度の段階を増やすと、応答をより正確に評価できます。

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Expression of three genes was measured in two specialized cell types from the same organism.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Identify the gene with the largest difference in expression between the two cell types.
markscheme: Gene K.
markschemeJa: 遺伝子K。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain how different gene-expression patterns can lead to specialized cell structure and function.
markscheme: Different genes being expressed cause different proteins to be produced in the two cell types.
Different proteins alter structures, organelle abundance, membrane properties and metabolic activities, producing different specialized functions.
markschemeJa: 異なる遺伝子が発現することで、2つの細胞型で異なるタンパク質がつくられる。
異なるタンパク質が構造、オルガネラ量、膜特性、代謝活動を変え、異なる特殊化機能を生じる。
parts.modelAnswer: Different expression patterns produce different proteins, which determine cell structures and biochemical activities suited to different functions.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 異なる発現パターンによって異なるタンパク質がつくられ、それが細胞構造や生化学的活動を変えて異なる機能に適応させます。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain why the two cell types can have very different expression patterns even though they contain the same genome.
markscheme: Most somatic cells contain the same genes, but regulatory mechanisms activate or suppress different genes in different cell types.
Cell differentiation establishes and maintains these different patterns of gene expression.
markschemeJa: 多くの体細胞は同じ遺伝子をもつが、調節機構により細胞型ごとに異なる遺伝子が活性化・抑制される。
細胞分化によってこれらの異なる遺伝子発現パターンが形成・維持される。
parts.modelAnswer: They share the same genome, but regulation during differentiation turns different genes on or off in each cell type.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 同じゲノムを持っていても、分化過程の調節によって細胞型ごとに異なる遺伝子がオン・オフになります。

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: The same homologous DNA region was compared among four species.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Identify the pair of species that is most closely related according to the DNA data.
markscheme: Species P and Q.
markschemeJa: 種PとQ。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Calculate the difference between the number of nucleotide differences for P–S and P–Q.
markscheme: 45 − 8 = 37 nucleotide differences.

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain why fewer differences in a homologous DNA sequence can support the conclusion that two species share a more recent common ancestor.
markscheme: Mutations accumulate in DNA lineages over evolutionary time.
Fewer sequence differences generally indicate less time since divergence from a common ancestral sequence, assuming comparable evolutionary rates.
markschemeJa: DNA系統では進化の時間とともに突然変異が蓄積する。
進化速度が比較可能なら、配列差が少ないほど共通祖先から分岐してからの時間が短いと考えられる。
parts.modelAnswer: Mutations accumulate after lineages diverge, so fewer differences in the same homologous region generally suggest that the lineages separated more recently.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 系統が分岐した後に突然変異が蓄積するため、同じ相同領域の差が少ないほど、より最近分岐したと考えられます。

parts.label: (d)
parts.question: Evaluate the use of this single DNA region as the only evidence for evolutionary relationships among the four species.
markscheme: A DNA comparison provides objective molecular evidence, but one short region may not represent the evolutionary history of the whole genome.
A stronger conclusion would use multiple independent DNA regions and other evidence such as morphology, fossils or reproductive/ecological data.
markschemeJa: DNA比較は客観的な分子証拠になるが、1つの短い領域だけではゲノム全体の進化史を代表しない可能性がある。
複数の独立したDNA領域と、形態、化石、生殖・生態データなど他の証拠を組み合わせると結論が強くなる。
parts.modelAnswer: The DNA region is useful molecular evidence, but one region alone may be unrepresentative. Multiple loci and independent evidence would give a more robust phylogenetic conclusion.
parts.modelAnswerJa: このDNA領域は有用な分子証拠ですが、1領域だけでは代表性に限界があります。複数領域と独立した証拠を組み合わせる方が信頼性が高まります。

stimulus.title: Nucleotide differences in the same DNA region

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Two insect populations experienced different environments over 20 generations.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Describe the change in allele X frequency in the dry environment.
markscheme: Allele X frequency increases steadily from 0.12 at generation 0 to 0.76 at generation 20.
The increase becomes substantial over successive generations rather than occurring as a single-step change.
markschemeJa: 乾燥環境ではXの頻度が世代0の0.12から世代20の0.76まで継続的に増加する。
変化は一度に起こるのではなく、複数世代にわたり大きくなる。
parts.modelAnswer: Allele X rises steadily from 0.12 to 0.76 across 20 generations.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 対立遺伝子Xは20世代で0.12から0.76へ継続的に増加します。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Compare the allele-frequency pattern in the dry and moist environments.
markscheme: Allele X rises strongly in the dry environment but remains close to the starting frequency in the moist environment.
markschemeJa: Xは乾燥環境で大きく増えるが、湿潤環境では開始頻度付近にとどまる。
parts.modelAnswer: X increases strongly in the dry environment but changes little in the moist environment.
parts.modelAnswerJa: Xは乾燥環境では大きく増えますが、湿潤環境ではほとんど変化しません。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain how natural selection could produce the observed difference between environments.
markscheme: If allele X increases survival or reproductive success in the dry environment, carriers contribute more offspring to the next generation.
Because the advantage depends on environment, the selection pressure may be weak or absent in the moist environment, so allele frequency changes little there.
markschemeJa: Xが乾燥環境で生存・繁殖成功を高めるなら、保有個体が次世代へより多くの子孫を残す。
利点が環境依存なら湿潤環境では選択圧が弱い・ないため、頻度はほとんど変化しない。
parts.modelAnswer: If X improves fitness in dry conditions, carriers leave more offspring and X becomes more common. If it gives little advantage in moist conditions, its frequency changes much less there.
parts.modelAnswerJa: Xが乾燥条件で適応度を高めれば保有個体がより多く繁殖し、Xが増えます。湿潤条件で利点が小さければ頻度変化も小さくなります。

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Answer all parts about DNA composition and replication.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: A double-stranded DNA sample contains 18% guanine. Calculate the expected percentages of cytosine and adenine.
markscheme: Cytosine is 18% because guanine pairs with cytosine.
G + C = 36%, leaving 64% for A + T; adenine is therefore 32%.
markschemeJa: グアニンとシトシンは対になるため、シトシンは18%。
G+C＝36%なのでA+Tは64%、したがってアデニンは32%。
parts.modelAnswerJa: シトシン18%、アデニン32%です。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain how complementary base pairing contributes to accurate DNA replication.
markscheme: Each parental strand acts as a template, and exposed bases pair specifically with complementary nucleotides.
A pairs with T and C pairs with G, so the nucleotide sequence of each new strand is determined by the template sequence.
markschemeJa: 各親鎖が鋳型となり、露出した塩基に相補的ヌクレオチドが特異的に結合する。
AはT、CはGと対合するため、新生鎖の塩基配列は鋳型配列によって決まる。
parts.modelAnswer: Each parental strand is a template. Specific A–T and C–G pairing determines the sequence of the new complementary strand.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 各親鎖が鋳型となり、A-T、C-Gの特異的な対合によって新しい相補鎖の配列が決まります。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain why DNA replication is described as semi-conservative.
markscheme: The two parental DNA strands separate before new complementary strands are synthesized.
Each daughter DNA molecule contains one parental strand and one newly synthesized strand.
markschemeJa: 親DNAの2本鎖が分離してから新しい相補鎖が合成される。
複製後の各DNA分子は親由来の鎖1本と新生鎖1本を含む。
parts.modelAnswer: The parental strands separate and each templates a new strand, so each daughter molecule contains one old strand and one new strand.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 親鎖が分かれてそれぞれ新生鎖の鋳型となるため、各娘DNAは親鎖1本と新生鎖1本を含みます。
